newsitem.title: CHILE: German colony members leave Chile for Argentina.
newsitem.headline: German colony members leave Chile for Argentina.

text.p: Hartmut Hopp, one of the leaders of a secretive German colony in southern Chile, has left the country accompanied by four other settlers, police said on Friday.
Police reported that the group, which included the adopted daughter of the colony's fugitive chief Paul Schaefer as well as Hopp's wife and son, flew to the city of Mendoza in Argentina.
Spokesmen for Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony), which is 320 kilometres (200 miles) south of Santiago, said the settlers were going on holiday.
Local media reported that Hopp, widely regarded as the successor to Schaefer, was to appear in court on Thursday in a case relating to the adoption of his 13-year old son Michael.

The settlers left Chile the same day as two young fugitives from the colony were giving evidence in the town of Parral to a judge investigating allegations that Schaefer sexually abused at least five boys at the colony's boarding school.
He and other leaders also were accused of illegal detention of children, obstruction of justice and tax fraud.
Tobias Muller, a 24-year-old German, and Chilean Gonzalo Luna escaped from the settlement last week and have been staying at a German diplomat's house in Santiago.
A series of police raids in recent months at the heavily armed colony failed to find any trace of the 76-year-old Schaefer, was not seen in public in recent years.
Newspaper La Tercera reported Muller and Luna told the judge that Schaefer was holed up in the enclave that he founded in 1961 after fleeing from Germany.
